Adjust correction and ghosting: Hugging Face comparisons

Findings

  • Adjust correction (12% feather) clearly reduces ghosting on both vessels. Total mismatch (ghosting proxy) drops at every join: LACMA 168596 14.5/9.0/6.5 → 4.2/5.2/5.3 px; Met 310364 at all 8 joins (e.g. 12.9 → 9.7, 6.7 → 4.0, 5.0 → 2.1). The crops confirm it: doubled ink strokes in the baseline (LACMA joins 0↔1 and 1↔2; Met at every join, worst 3↔7, 4↔7, 1↔5) are gone or much reduced.
  • Vertical mismatch (the warp's target) improves at most joins but not all. LACMA: 1.90 → 0.59 at 0↔1, but 1.34 → 1.90 and 0.80 → 1.19 at the other two. Met: better at 5 of 8 joins (e.g. 4.66 → 1.08, 4.93 → 1.79), slightly worse at 3 (0.89 → 0.98, 1.37 → 1.98, 1.05 → 1.15). The visual gain comes mostly from less total mismatch, not only vertical.
  • 4% feathering does not help. Met: indistinguishable from 12% in numbers and crops; no obvious harder exposure seams either. LACMA: join 2↔3 got much worse (vertical 1.19 → 7.97 px, total 5.2 → 17.6) and the right serpent is visibly doubled. With one Space run per arm, this may be the Space placing that piece differently rather than feathering itself; a repeat run would tell.
  • Residual ghosting remains on Met at joins 3↔7 and 4↔7, which involve views 2 and 3 (positions 05 and 09 in the order). Those views register weakly to the returned panorama (≈215–350 inliers vs thousands for the others), so their joins' numbers are also the least reliable.
  • No files were missing. All six panoramas are actual Space outputs (pre-Refine); crops are centred on each arm's own measured overlap centre, so they show the same paint but not identical pixels.

Pre-Refine panoramas returned by the Space. Vertical = median vertical mismatch of matched landmarks across the join (evaluates the warp); total = median total mismatch (ghosting-risk proxy). Numbers alone don't prove visible ghosting: check the crops for doubled strokes.
